name: Sharai
overview: Sharai is a male descendant of Bani mentioned in the book of Ezra. His unique attribute is that he had married a foreign wife, a fact recorded in Ezra 10:40. There is no additional information about his tribe or other personal details.
namesAndTitles: The name Sharai appears only once in Scripture, specifically in Ezra 10:40. No special meaning or divine origin is given for this proper name in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Sharai is explicitly identified as a descendant of Bani, establishing a familial connection within the post-exilic community. Beyond this, Scripture does not record any further family relationships for him.
scriptureSignificance: Sharai's mention in Ezra 10:40 highlights the issue of intermarriage with foreign wives among the returned exiles. His inclusion among those who had taken foreign wives underscores the challenges faced by Israel in maintaining covenantal purity during the restoration period. This reflects the broader narrative of Ezra addressing the need for faithfulness to God's commands in the community.
